items.stem: Which statement best captures the relationship between compliance and security?

options.text: Compliance is a baseline; it does not by itself guarantee security
options.rationale: Correct: meeting requirements is necessary but not sufficient for security.
An organisation can be compliant yet still insecure.
Compliance obligations remain regardless of security maturity.
Compliance is often a floor, not a ceiling.

items.explanation: Correct: compliance is a baseline and does not alone guarantee security.

items.stem: Which TWO are valid ways to treat an identified risk? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: mitigation reduces likelihood or impact.

options.text: Transfer it, for example through insurance
options.rationale: Correct: transfer shifts financial impact to another party.

options.text: Ignore it and hope it does not happen
options.rationale: Ignoring is not a managed treatment; acceptance must be deliberate and documented.

options.text: Hide it from the risk register

items.explanation: Correct: mitigation and transfer are both valid risk treatments.

items.stem: Why can point-in-time compliance evidence be misleading?

options.text: Controls may be met during the audit but neglected the rest of the year
options.rationale: Correct: a snapshot does not prove controls operate continuously.
The issue is coverage over time, not inherent fraud.
Auditors do review evidence; the concern is its time coverage.

options.text: Compliance has no relationship to controls
options.rationale: Compliance is evidenced precisely through controls.

items.explanation: Correct: a snapshot can hide that controls lapse outside the audit window.
